summary: ERRPROC is the standard Error Processing subroutine used across the system. Called with an error request (program id, category, code, severity, text, details), it appends a timestamped 400-byte record to a sequential error-log file, also prints a formatted error block to the job log, and returns the severity as the return code. It is the common 'log this error' service that most programs CALL from their 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CALL 1000-INITIALIZE
CALL 2000-PROCESS-ERROR
CALL 3000-TERMINATE
RETURN to caller (GOBACK)

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CLEAR WS-WORK-AREAS
ACCEPT WS-FORMATTED-TIME FROM TIME STAMP
OPEN ERROR-LOG for append (EXTEND)
IF open NOT success THEN DISPLAY 'Error opening log file' END IF
branches: IF log open failed -> display (continues anyway)

annotations.note: On open failure it only DISPLAYs and keeps going — a later WRITE would then fail too; the error handler is not itself fail-safe.

paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-ERROR
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET ERR-* fields from the request: timestamp, program, category, code, severity, text, details
CALL 2100-WRITE-LOG
CALL 2200-DISPLAY-ERROR
SET LS-RETURN-CODE = LS-SEVERITY   -- echo severity back to caller

paragraphs.name: 2100-WRITE-LOG
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET LOG-DATA = ERR-MESSAGE
WRITE ERROR-LOG-RECORD
IF write NOT success THEN DISPLAY 'Error writing to log' END IF

paragraphs.name: 2200-DISPLAY-ERROR
paragraphs.pseudocode: DISPLAY a formatted error block to the job log: timestamp, program, category, code, severity, message, details (framed with '===' separators)

usage.note: Produced by Claude Code in-session; no API call, no key, no token cost.
